anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De Oratione exists (only copyrighted Greer/O'Meara/Oulton-Chadwick); nothing to compare against. Sense checked against the Greek and cited Scripture wording.

apparatus: 'Would that also in the Holy Spirit' hedge kept verbatim.
Matthew/Luke texts quoted in full as Origen prints them (Lk without doxology or deliverance clause).
Mark searched: 'not even a trace' — Origen's explicit negative result.

choices.why: hupographō/hupotupoō = sketch/outline a model; the Lord's Prayer is a pattern, matching Origen's 'forms' treatment later.
athlos = athletic contest; exposition is labor/sport — consistent with Origen's agon imagery throughout.

pass_a_gloss: Transition chapter: sufficiency claim under grace through Christ (with pneumatological hedge submitted to readers' judgment), then the synoptic problem — Matthew's and Luke's wordings printed in full, shown to differ in wording and occasion (mountain multitude vs certain place, single asking disciple), best taken as different prayers with common parts; Mark contains no Lord's Prayer at all.
